items.title: Taming Typography: Building a Modern CSS Reset
items.desc: Stu created tidy-typography.css: a style reset for taming typography with modern CSS features for everything from fluid typography and vertical rhythm, to hyphens and variable fonts. Taming Typography: Building a Modern CSS Reset originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.full: NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle. CSS can now make choices about type that used to sit outside a reset . text-wrap: pretty can prevent a stranded word, container query units can scale a heading to the column it occupies, and text-box can trim the half-leading built into a line box. Some of these features are experimental and browser support is uneven, so they need guardrails rather than blind inclusion. I’ve put together tidy-typography.css , which gathers the useful parts into a default stylesheet: rendering and fallback rules, fluid sizing, vertical rhythm, wrapping, hyphenation, and OpenType detail. Use it whole, or take the declaration that solves the particular irritation in front of you. I’ll walk you through all the details in this article and give you the full code at the end. Rendering and fallback sanity html { -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; font-synthesis: none; -moz-text-size-adjust: none; -webkit-text-size-adjust: none; text-size-adjust: none; } body { font-size-adjust: from-font; } font-synthesis: none stops a browser from inventing bold or italic when the family lacks that face. The smoothing and text-rendering declarations are rendering hints, mainly for WebKit; results still vary by platform. text-size-adjust disables mobile font inflation that can make a deliberately sized layout jump on rotation. font-size-adjust: from-font uses font metrics to reduce the apparent size change while a fallback swaps for a webfont. (As with other snippets in this article, this ⁠ :root block is a partial excerpt the final stylesheet combines it with additional custom properties defined later on.) Fluid typography Viewport-based fluid type does not know how wide its element is. A heading in a narrow sidebar can therefore scale as though it fills the viewport. .article-container { container-type: inline-size; } :root { --step-0: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 1cqi, 1.125rem); --step-3: clamp(2rem, 1.6rem + 3cqi, 2.75rem); } container-type: inline-size makes the wrapper a container query , so its children can use cqi : a unit based on the container rather than the viewport. Replacing vw in clamp() lets the same heading scale appropriately in an article column or a 300px sidebar without component-specific media queries. Vertical rhythm: trim the half-leading :heading, p, blockquote, figcaption, li { text-box-trim: trim-both; text-box-edge: cap alphabetic; /* shorthand: text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic; */ } line-height includes space above the cap-height and below the baseline: half-leading. It becomes obvious when text must align tightly with another element. text-box-trim removes it, while text-box-edge measures from capital-letter caps to the alphabetic baseline. This is a metrics-aware alternative to font-specific negative-margin nudges. @supports selector(:heading) { :heading { text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic; } } Selectors Level 5 proposes :heading , matching h1 to h6 and [role="heading"] . It has not landed in browsers, so keep it behind an @supports selector() check. Balanced headlines, orphan-free paragraphs :heading, blockquote, figcaption { text-wrap: balance; } p, li, dd

items.title: Welcome Drip and Sleeknote to the WPBeginner Family of Products
items.desc: Today, I’m extremely excited to share that Drip and Sleeknote are joining the Awesome Motive network, and they’re now part of the WPBeginner family of products. Drip is an email marketing and automation platform designed for small businesses, from content creators to online stores. More…
items.full: Today, I’m extremely excited to share that Drip and Sleeknote are joining the Awesome Motive network, and they’re now part of the WPBeginner family of products . Drip is an email marketing and automation platform designed for small businesses, from content creators to online stores. More than 6,000 brands use Drip to turn first-time visitors into subscribers, buyers, and repeat customers. On the other hand, Sleeknote is a conversion optimization tool that turns your website visitors into subscribers and customers with popups, slide-ins, sticky bars, and more. Together, Sleeknote and Drip help you drive more conversions by reaching customers wherever they engage with your brand, whether that’s on your website, in their email inbox, or through SMS. Drip gives small businesses and ecommerce store owners everything they need to grow sales with email, without the high costs. It works with WooCommerce, Shopify, and BigCommerce. That means your store data flows straight into your email marketing tool, so you can personalize your messages based on what your customers actually do and buy. We’ve been using Drip to power the email marketing on WPBeginner and our product brands for many years, so I’ve seen firsthand how much revenue a good email setup can bring in. Sleeknote helps you get more email signups and sales from the traffic you already have. You can control exactly who sees each campaign and when. For example, you can target visitors based on the pages they view, where they came from, whether they’re new or returning, and what’s in their cart, so every message feels relevant instead of random. Sleeknote is free for all users on Drip as part of the Drip forms. Let’s take a detailed look. Drip comes with a drag-and-drop visual workflow builder. You can use it to create anything from a single automated email to a complex multi-step campaign. You don’t have to start from scratch, either. You can choose from Drip’s extensive ready-made workflow templates and install them on your account with a single click. You can easily customize each workflow by adding decisions, delays, and goals to guide subscribers along the right path. You can even split-test different paths to see which ones generate more revenue. Drip comes with a free MCP connector on every plan. It lets you connect AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT directly to your Drip account. Simply put, you can ask your AI which campaign made the most money last month or have it draft and schedule your next campaign. Some messages work better as a text than an email, like a flash sale that ends tonight or a cart a shopper left a few minutes ago. Drip now has built-in SMS marketing for stores in the United States (other countries coming soon). You can run your email and text campaigns from the same account, using the same customer data and segments. You can send one-off text campaigns to any segment, or add SMS steps to your workflows. For example, your abandoned cart workflow can send a reminder email first, then follow up with a text if the shopper still hasn’t checked out. The SMS builder counts your characters as you type, lets you personalize each message, and adds the required opt-out language

items.title: Dive into the Ipsum WordPress theme, and how to extend it
items.desc: With WordPress 7.2 launching in December, a new default theme is on the way. Marking a departure from tradition, it drops the usual calendar-year naming scheme ...
items.full: With WordPress 7.2 launching in December, a new default theme is on the way. Marking a departure from tradition, it drops the usual calendar-year naming scheme in favor of a more meaningful name. Dubbed Ipsum , this new addition is a minimalist, lightweight, and modular block theme built for Full Site Editing (FSE) and strictly aligned with modern Block Editor standards. As the name suggests, Ipsum streamlines the blogging experience and works out of the box the moment you start writing. Its design is understated in every detail, from subtle dotted underlines to the bundled typography and a curated set of style variations , focused on accessibility and readability. Don’t let its minimalist nature fool you, though. Ipsum provides the ideal blank canvas to bring your creative vision as a blogger to life. Let’s dive into the latest default theme and explore how to get the most out of it using native WordPress features. Ipsum features a minimalist design with a strong focus on readability. The new default theme defines six shades of gray with high-contrast combinations alongside a single accent color. The default background ( #fcfcfc ) and body text ( #000000bf ) achieve a contrast ratio (CR) of 10.26:1, easily earning a WCAG AAA rating. Ipsum supports native WordPress keyboard navigation, displaying a “Skip to content” link on every page. This allows users navigating with the Tab key to jump straight to the main content without having to cycle through header navigation links. The theme also highlights focused links with its accent color, letting keyboard users quickly identify the active element. Typography plays a major role in making Ipsum easy on the eyes, offering five preset font sizes and supporting fluid typography . Links are distinguished only by a subtle dotted underline. While aligned with the theme’s minimalist aesthetic, this might make them hard to spot depending on the page’s color conditions. That said, links remain easy to identify during keyboard navigation thanks to the accent-colored focus outline. Now, let’s take a closer look at Ipsum’s specific features. Ipsum includes a built-in set of templates that delegate page layouts to internal patterns. As an example, here is the markup of the page.html template: <!-- wp:pattern {"slug":"ipsum/hidden-page"} /--> This single line of code calls the hidden pattern hidden-page.php , which controls the layout and sets the required metadata: /** * Title: Pages * Slug: ipsum/hidden-page * Template Types: page * Inserter: no * * @package Ipsum * @since Ipsum 1.0 */ The theme registers custom template variants, such as index-sidebar and archive-sidebar , directly via PHP so you can select them in the Site Editor. As of now, roughly 60 patterns are available to help you build and format your content. While some of these patterns are reserved (hidden) for the theme’s core templates, the majority are fully accessible for you to use in your pages. An interesting technical detail for developers is how patterns implement the Block Bindings API . items.title: Making Immersive LLM Chat Experiences More Accessible
items.desc: As LLM chat patterns become more widespread, making them accessible is essential to ensuring everyone can access the information, tools, and opportunities they offer. Drawing on his work improving these interfaces, Eric Bailey shares practical ways to make chat-based experiences on the web more accessible and usable for people who rely on assistive technology.
items.full: About The Author Eric is a Boston-based designer who helps create straightforward solutions that address a person’s practical, physical, cognitive, and emotional needs. More about Eric ↬ Weekly tips on front-end & UX . Trusted by 182,000+ folks. Design Patterns For AI Interfaces with Vitaly Friedman Designing For Complex UI Masterclass with Vitaly Friedman Meet AI 2027 Conference, December 1, 2026. Building Modern HTML Emails with Rémi Parmentier As LLM chat patterns become more widespread, making them accessible is essential to ensuring everyone can access the information, tools, and opportunities they offer. Drawing on his work improving these interfaces, Eric Bailey shares practical ways to make chat-based experiences on the web more accessible and usable for people who rely on assistive technology. I have had the privilege of helping to improve the accessibility of multiple immersive LLM chat experiences in the course of my career. Now I want to share this knowledge with you. Accessibility is a core part of a functional digital experience. As the LLM chat pattern continues to spread like wildfire across the web, we risk excluding people if these experiences are not built with accessibility as a core consideration. It is also worth re-mentioning what “exclusion” means here : It’s the loss of knowledge, the loss of opportunity, the loss of utility, the loss of employability, the loss of entertainment, and more. “Immersive LLM chat experience” is a catch-all term for full-screen experiences like Claude , ChatGPT , GitHub Copilot , Gemini , America.gov , Glean , and other similar websites and web apps: The majority of what this post covers applies to both web apps and native apps . This is because these experiences are typically built using web technologies, then placed in a native wrapper via frameworks such as Electron or Tauri . Immersive LLM chat experiences are not patterns such as a pop-up chat, inline text generation utilities, or summarization tools. These simpler applications of LLM technology will have different considerations and expectations. Instead, this is a starting point for making those other experiences accessible. There is nothing special about chat-based UIs when viewed via the lens of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines . They are interactive experiences, built using web technologies. The losses I’ve described — and the legal liability associated with them — are access barriers in the same way any other web content can be an access barrier. I would also like to mention the social model of disability here: the idea that exclusion can be created by the built environment. For example, consider an elevated entryway that uses a gently sloping ramp in place of stairs. Built environments also extend to digital experiences , and the social model also applies here. The main activities undertaken to operate an LLM chat are already well-established: It is how we facilitate — or fail to facilitate — those interactions that’s the salient bit. items.title: Anthropic's text watermark is easy to bypass on several older Claude models
items.desc: Anthropic is rolling out text watermarks to four more Claude models ahead of the EU AI Act's December deadline. But on older models like Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, API users can disable the watermark by changing a single sampling parameter. Anthropic's response to the loophole? A compliance warning. The article Anthropic's text watermark is easy to bypass on several older Claude models appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Update, November 4, 2026: Anthropic emailed API customers again about a second round of watermark retrofits. Starting November 16, 2026, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 will all get text watermarking. On Amazon Bedrock, the rollout may take a few extra days. Claude Opus 4.6 was originally part of the first wave and should have gotten the watermark on November 3. Anthropic explicitly confirms the delay to November 16 but gives no reason. The other three first-wave models, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Sonnet 4.6, don't show up in the new email so their rollout likely went ahead on November 3 as planned. Ad Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 are three models that weren't part of the previous announcement. All four models in this wave share the same sampling restriction: the watermark only applies when temperature , top_p , and top_k are set to their defaults. In the first wave, that limit only hit two of four models (Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6). Ad Original article, October 31, 2026: Anthropic is expanding its text watermark to four more Claude models, but API users can dodge the mark on two of them by tweaking a single sampling parameter. Ad In an email to API customers, Anthropic said it will watermark Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Sonnet 4.6. Newer models like Claude Opus 5.5 already carry the mark, and the rollout on Amazon Bedrock may take a few extra days. Anthropic calls the watermark an "imperceptible pattern in word choice" that doesn't change meaning, quality, or readability. The company says it adds no extra characters or tokens, doesn't affect pricing or request and response formats, and barely slows output speed. Anthropic also says the watermark "contains no information about the user, their organization, or their conversations with Claude." Ad On Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6, Anthropic says the watermark kicks in only when developers leave the three sampling parameters at their default values. Those parameters, temperature , top_p , and top_k , control how much randomness the model uses when picking words. A minor tweak to any one of them is enough to dodge the watermark. Anthropic warns in its email that "If you rely on the watermark for your own compliance, keep these settings at their defaults." Ad The email doesn't mention that caveat for Claude Mythos 5 or Claude Opus 4.7, which suggests the watermark applies to those models regardless of sampling settings. But the loophole on the older models is still notable, since Opus 4.6 remains Anthropic's best writing model , ahead of even Opus 5.5. Anthropic has a detection API in private preview for verifying the watermark and offers more details on its content labeling information page . Anthropic points to the EU AI Act's December deadline as the reason it's watermarking older models now. Every model released after Aug. 2, 2026, shipped with the watermark on day one, while older models are getting it in stages. items.title: OpenAI acquires Pierre Computer Company to make Git keep up with AI coding agents
items.desc: OpenAI is buying Pierre Computer Company, the startup whose libraries already power the coding agent Codex. Combined with OpenAI's recently launched Git backend Pando, the deal shows the company is building out its infrastructure for developers and AI agents working side by side. The article OpenAI acquires Pierre Computer Company to make Git keep up with AI coding agents appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI is buying Pierre Computer Company, Inc., the startup behind Code Storage and several open-source tools. Pierre's libraries already power OpenAI's coding agent Codex. "Trees" handles fast project file navigation, "Diffs" displays code changes and lets users fix bugs right in the diff view, and "Highlights" is a real-time syntax highlighter that works as developers type or an AI agent generates code. Code Storage stores code and tracks history through Git. OpenAI says the acquisition is about making Git workflows work better when developers and AI agents are writing code side by side. As agents handle more tasks in parallel, the tooling around Git has to keep up. OpenAI already runs Pando , its own version control backend built for both developers and agents. Pierre's open-source projects will stay open source. The deal still needs regulatory approval. items.title: Schools that turn off Google's AI will lose search too starting in 2027
items.desc: Starting in 2027, Google plans to turn off AI features in its school products by default, letting schools decide what to enable. The catch: schools that block AI entirely on their devices will also lose access to Google Search, since the two systems are now too deeply intertwined to separate. Given Google's grip on the US school market, that "choice" doesn't leave schools with much room to maneuver. The article Schools that turn off Google's AI will lose search too starting in 2027 appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Starting in early 2027, Google will give schools an ultimatum: accept AI for students or lose access to Google Search entirely. Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Google Search will all be off by default for student accounts. Schools can turn each one on individually. But a version of search without AI? That's no longer on the table. The New York Times broke the story first. Google's vice president for education, Chris Phillips, said search and AI have become too tightly fused to pull apart. Google recently flipped AI features on by default inside its learning platform Classroom for schools with Gemini access. That move drew backlash, and the company is now reversing course. Schools that choose to enable search will get two flavors: search with full AI overviews and AI chat, or search with "Guided Learning," a mode designed to steer students toward answers rather than hand them over directly. None of this happens in a vacuum. Google dominates the US school market with Chromebooks, Gmail, and Classroom. Education professor Morgan Polikoff called the move a textbook case of the tech industry shoving AI onto people whether they want it or not. The country's two largest school districts, New York City and Los Angeles, had already pulled back on AI for students in September. Los Angeles specifically wanted to keep using Google Search without AI overviews. Google won't let them. OpenAIs GPT-6 Cyber can both break into systems and propose how to fix them
items.desc: With GPT-6 Cyber, OpenAI is introducing an AI model built to find security vulnerabilities in software, develop exploits, and suggest patches. According to OpenAI, it has already found 81 previously unknown vulnerabilities in Firefox and developed 948 working exploits in the Linux kernel, significantly more than its predecessor. The article OpenAIs GPT-6 Cyber can both break into systems and propose how to fix them appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, an AI model trained specifically to hunt for security vulnerabilities in software. OpenAI says the model can find flaws, build working exploits, and suggest patches. It's also supposed to stay within its assigned boundaries, something some OpenAI models have struggled with in recent months . The firm says it trained GPT-6 Cyber to respect its operational guardrails, using, among other things, a honeypot inspired by the Hugging Face incident . Without any special safety instructions, GPT-6 Cyber avoided boundary violations in 99.93 percent of cases, up from 94.49 percent for its predecessor. With safety instructions enabled, the model stayed within bounds in 100 percent of tests. Overall, OpenAI rates GPT-6 Cyber as "Critical" in the cybersecurity category of its own Preparedness Framework , the same rating it gave to GPT-6 Astra, the "base" model . Ad On ExploitGym, a benchmark that tests whether a model can exploit a given vulnerability in a remote system, GPT-6 Cyber scores 48.5 percent according to OpenAI, compared to 32.1 percent for its predecessor GPT-5.6 Cyber. On a new test for finding vulnerabilities in web apps without access to source code, OpenAI reports a hit rate of 40.3 percent, versus 32.0 percent for GPT-6 Astra, the standard model without cyber training. Ad Full results are available in the system card . All benchmark numbers come from OpenAI itself. No independent testing of the model has been published so far. GPT-6 Cyber has already produced results in real-world security research, according to OpenAI. In a targeted campaign, the model found 81 previously unknown severe vulnerabilities in Firefox , even though the browser had already been tested with earlier AI models. The model also showed that 30 already-known issues were more severe than previously thought. Mozilla accepted the reports and has already shipped fixes. Ad In the Linux kernel, GPT-6 Cyber reproduced 1,724 security vulnerabilities and developed working exploits for 948 of them, more than five times the 166 that GPT-5.6 Sol managed under the same conditions, according to OpenAI. 304 critical findings were reported to Linux maintainers along with suggested fixes, the company says. For the Linux kernel campaign , OpenAI built a dedicated automated system of scout and analyst agents. They first scanned roughly 5,034 security-relevant locations in the kernel, about seven percent of the total codebase, then filtered those down to 2,308 candidates and confirmed 1,724 vulnerabilities in isolated virtual machines. From there, the system developed the 948 working exploits that OpenAI had already reported. The entire run cost $1,213,430 in compute, according to OpenAI, which works out to $1,279 per exploit. For comparison, programs like Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN have historically paid between $20,000 and $70,000 per comparable finding as a bounty. Ad The agents used at least ten novel attack techniques that were previously unknown even to external kernel security experts, OpenAI says.
